offence_severity: 5 years rigorous imprisonment to 10 years rigorous imprisonment with fine
physical_harm: Six knife blows causing serious injuries leading to death
premeditation_planning: No premeditation, act done in heat of passion
motive: Trivial motive of smoke blown on face
key_evidence_accepted: The evidence clearly establishes that the appellant assaulted the deceased without any premeditation. The whole incident took place suddenly and, in the heat of passion, a sudden quarrel started as the deceased, while smoking, blew smoke on the face of the appellant. Resultantly, the appellant got enraged. He told him that he was senior in age and thus should not smoke in his presence much less blow the smoke towards him. Then a sudden physical fight started between them, in which the appellant, in heat of passion, gave six knife blows to the deceased on different parts of his body.
witness_credibility: The evidence of PW-11 and PW-12 (eye-witnesses) would establish that the appellant and others including deceased Hitesh Thakur had gathered at the spot for a drink party arranged at the instance of Hitesh Thakur. They had consumed drinks when the incident took place. Soon after assaulting Hitesh Thakur by knife, when the appellant realised that Hitesh has been badly injured, he offered him water and took him to the hospital along with his other friends. He was in the hospital till Hitesh Thakur succumbed to the injuries. He had also informed the father of Hitesh on telephone and called him to the hospital.
post_offence_conduct: After realising his mistake, he immediately offered water to Hitesh Thakur and also took him to hospital and stayed there till his last rites were performed. PW-2 father of deceased Hitesh Thakur also corroborates the position that the appellant had contacted him to inform that Hitesh had been brought to the hospital in serious condition.
trial_duration: Offence: 27.07.2011; Trial judgment: 31.12.2014; High Court decision: 01.04.2016; Supreme Court decision: 19.01.2018
legal_representation: Aditya Dhawan, Ms. Kiran Dhawan, Chander Shekhar Ashri, Advs. for the Appellant; D. K. Thakur, AAG, Shariq Ahmed, Ms. Taiba Khan, Ajay Marwah, Advs. for the Respondents
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted under s.304 Part II; High Court: Convicted under s.302; Supreme Court: Partly allowed appeals, restored Trial Court's conviction under s.304 Part II with enhanced sentence
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant caused six injuries to the deceased by attacking him with a knife on the fateful night in the presence of their friends who had gathered at the house of accused no.2 for celebrating a drink party arranged at the behest of the deceased. The deceased succumbed to the injuries caused by the appellant.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the appellant acted in the heat of passion without premeditation and did not intend to cause the death of the deceased. The appellant offered water to the deceased, took him to the hospital, and stayed until the deceased's last rites were performed, indicating no intention to cause death.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that culpable homicide not amounting to murder is applicable when the act is committed in the heat of passion without premeditation and without taking undue advantage or acting in a cruel manner.
precedent_relied_upon: Surain Singh v. State of Punjab (2017) 5 SCC 796
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the nature of the offence and the trivial reason for the appellant's rage and assault, along with the use of a knife and multiple blows, did not warrant a light punishment. The sentence period should not be less than 10 years imprisonment with fine to meet the ends of justice.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The court weighed the appellant's actions in the heat of passion, the lack of premeditation, and the fact that the appellant offered water to the deceased and took him to the hospital.
other_sentence_order: The appellant was sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for 10 years with a fine of Rs.10,000/-, in default to undergo further imprisonment for one year. The appellant is entitled to set off under Section 428 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
